summary: PATCH /api/v1/users/{username}: credentials carrying a scope (API keys) no longer get the 'editing your own profile' free pass; they need user.update in scope. Closes a hole where read-only keys could rename the owning account.

statements.why: The change tightens access (service.py:415 `if not scoped and ...`); nothing newly exposed. Still, the card hides that this is a security fix and a behaviour change for API-key users.

misses.what: Security fix: an API key scoped to nothing or only to reading could rename its owner's account (name/username) via PATCH /api/v1/users/{username}; scoped credentials now need user.update for that.

Behaviour change: existing API-key integrations that edit their own profile now get 403 unless the key is scoped with user.update (and, without the rbac feature, only superusers' keys can hold it). Browser sessions are unaffected.
